title: Condition "!is_inside_tree()" is true. Returning: Transform3D() erroneously reports as an error in 3D, not in 2D
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.4.1

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable - Freedesktop SDK 24.08 (Flatpak runtime) on X11 - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (radeonsi, raphael_mendocino, LLVM 19.1.7, DRM 3.63, 6.15.0-061500-generic) - AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D 8-Core Processor (16 threads)

### Issue description

A very annoying error message pops up when editing transform properties of orphan nodes in 3d that doesn't pop up for 2d. This error message is vestigial, as editing the transform works as expected. There are no options to disable this error message. Per the below forum discussion, the code that creates this error is cleaner and more straight forward than the intended(?) method.

https://forum.godotengine.org/t/adding-an-instantiated-scene-to-the-tree-correctly-creates-a-problem/57032/10

Right now, the way to fix this error message is to call _ready again manually after adding things to the scene just to perform transform edits in the proper order. I hope I don't need to explain how this is stupid.

Again, **editing transforms before putting the node in the scene works without issues - what is the point of this printing here?**
And also, **This doesn't happen in 2D, it has the same behavior but doesn't output the error and it's wonderful.**

What I'm seeking is at least a way to disable this ""error"" but ideally it should be removed.

### Steps to reproduce

```
var _new = Node3D.new()
_new.position = Vector3(1.0,0.0,0.0) #<-- error, even though behavior works with no issues
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Put this code in any function, when that function runs it'll error:
```
var _new = Node3D.new()
_new.position = Vector3(1.0,0.0,0.0) #<-- error, even though behavior works with no issues
```
